other_failure_modes.name: Log-Transform Bias in RMSE Optimization
other_failure_modes.description: Training a regression model on a log-transformed target and exponentiating the predictions yields the conditional median, not the conditional mean. When evaluated on the raw scale using RMSE (which penalizes deviations from the mean), this systematically underestimates the target expected value and incurs heavy quadratic penalties due to Jensen's inequality.

summary: The agent implements a robust 5-fold cross-validation pipeline combining LightGBM, XGBoost, CatBoost, and a PyTorch neural network, alongside sophisticated feature engineering and optimized blending. However, the solution suffers from a critical statistical flaw: predicting the conditional median via a log-transform while evaluating on the raw scale using RMSE, which severely degrades performance due to Jensen's inequality. Additionally, the agent introduces cross-fold leakage by fitting TF-IDF and SVD on the full training set before CV splitting, and applies transductive test-set transformations that violate standard predictive modeling assumptions.
